originalGroup.material:
The tail on the blue kite

Ben has a blue kite. On Saturday, he takes it to the park with Dad. The kite has a long yellow tail. Ben runs across the grass, and the kite goes up. Then the tail catches on a low branch. Dad helps him bring the kite down without pulling hard. The yellow paper has a small hole. At home, Ben puts a patch over it. He uses red paper because there is no yellow paper left. On Sunday, the kite flies again. Its tail now has one red spot. Ben likes being able to recognise his kite in the sky.

A chair for the teddy bear

Leo makes a chair for his teddy bear from a small cardboard box. He cuts a back and two arms, then covers the seat with cloth. The chair looks good, but it falls over when Teddy sits down. The tall flower by the gate

There is a tall sunflower beside our garden gate. My little sister calls it the garden sun. In the morning, she counts its big green leaves with me. Mum asks her to leave it for everyone to see. We draw a picture instead. My sister puts the picture above her desk. The real flower stays by the gate, where the post worker smiles at it every morning.

questions.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.
questions.prompt: Mr Green opens the card while driving.
questions.material:
A card for the bus driver

Our school bus driver is Mr Green. On Friday, our class makes him a thank-you card. We draw a yellow bus on the front. Inside, every child writes a name. I write mine in blue, but my friend Sam uses green. We give the card to Mr Green after he parks the bus at school. He does not open it while driving. At lunchtime, our teacher shows us a photograph. Mr Green is holding the card and smiling. He has put it on the little table in the staff room. Sam says a green name was a good choice for Mr Green.
questions.explanation: He explicitly does not; card given after parking.
